summary: @grabcad/user-license ships postinstall beacon exfiltrating host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package declares a postinstall script `node beacon.cjs` and an index.js that re-invokes the same beacon on require(). beacon.cjs collects os.hostname(), __dirname (the install path), process.cwd(), the Node.js version, and the package name, and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The package has no real functionality: module.exports is a Proxy whose get handler returns a no-op function for any property access, so consumers importing the real @grabcad scope name resolve silently against this shim. The combination of a dependency-confusion-shaped name under the @grabcad scope, an inert Proxy stub standing in for the advertised 'compatibility shim', and an automatic install-time and import-time beacon to an attacker-controlled bare-IP collector is a reconnaissance payload that identifies build systems whose internal @grabcad package name resolution leaks to the public npm registry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
